statements.text: The circle is the set of points of a plane which are at constant distance from a fixed point in the same plane.
The fixed point is called the centre of the circle and the constant distance is called the radius length.
A circle is usually denoted by its center: circle M means the circle whose center is point M.
The set of points inside the circle, like points M, D, E, ...
The set of points on the circle, like points A, B, C, ...
The set of points outside the circle, like points X, Y, Z, ...
Surface of the circle: the set of points of the circle ∪ the set of points inside the circle. Formula: $\text{circle} \cup \text{interior points}$
Radius of a circle: a line segment with one endpoint at the center and the other endpoint on the circle.
Two circles are congruent if their radii are equal in length.
The chord: a line segment whose end points are any two points on the circle.
Diameter: the chord passing through the center of the circle.

statements.text: Any straight line passing through the center of a circle is an axis of symmetry of it.

context.text: Imagine a baker cuts a round basbousa tray straight across, passing through the middle point of the tray, into two pieces. The two pieces match exactly, as if you folded one onto the other. She then tries a different straight cut through the middle, and again the two halves match. How many such cuts through the centre of a circle would give two matching halves, and what do we call each of these lines?

statements.text: From 1: the straight line passing through the center of the circle and the midpoint of any chord of it is perpendicular to this chord.
From 2: the straight line passing through the center of a circle and perpendicular to any chord of it bisects this chord.
From 3: the perpendicular bisector of any chord of a circle passes through the center of the circle.

context.text: Suppose a circular field has its centre at a pole $M$ and a radius of $5$ m. A straight fence $\overline{AB}$ is $8$ m long and has both ends on the edge of the field. A worker walks from the pole $M$ to the midpoint of the fence. How far is the pole from the fence, measured along the shortest path?

context.text: Yousef used the program, Google Earth, on his computer to study the geography of Egypt. Yousef noticed some green, circular areas next to the desert areas so, he asked his father about them.

The father Said: You learn that a drop of water means the source of life. Therefore, we should minimize the consumption of water in order to irrigate the land by the central irrigation method (sprinkle irrigation) in which, the wheels of the irrigation machine circle around a fixex point which draws those circles.
